investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.finding: Thin-fabric flames quench when ventilation drops toward ~2 cm/s, so ventilation speed, not buoyancy, decides whether a small fire survives.
investigations.hardwareRule: Expose ventilation speed as a flammability control variable: log cabin flow on every smoke alarm and provide a one-command HVAC park state.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: the quench-to-blow-off airflow band informs floor-level damper and stairwell-pressurisation logic that should starve a small fire instead of feeding it.
investigations.basis: Sourced: four BASS tests at 21% O2 and 5, 10, 11 and 19 cm/s (BASS-II Summary Report, Table 7.1).

investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids – II
investigations.finding: Materials burned at lower oxygen in microgravity than in normal gravity. Extinction came from radiative quenching below ~2 cm/s and from blow-off near 40 cm/s.
investigations.hardwareRule: Do not accept a 1g pass at face value. Add a low-speed (2–15 cm/s) forced-flow burn test and certify against the lower microgravity limit.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: BASS-II shows how a gentle air stream both rescues and kills a flame, so smoke-control fans can be tuned to avoid the speeds that sustain a fire.
investigations.basis: Sourced: PMMA rod tests at 13.6–22.2% O2 and 0–55 cm/s flow (Olson & Ferkul 2017; NTRS 20160000593). Test logs: NASA/TM-20210011385.

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire I–VI)
investigations.finding: In the large module the flame spread more slowly than in smaller microgravity tunnels, so small-sample results cannot simply be scaled up to spacecraft size.
investigations.hardwareRule: Qualify materials at spacecraft-relevant length scales, not only 5 cm coupons. Instrument heat release plus CO and CO2 rise, which outran temperature and pressure rise in Saffire VI.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: large-scale fabric burns give heat-release and fabric-char data that help engineers design lighter outer layers that resist flame growth rather than merely survive it.
investigations.basis: Partly sourced: flows of 5, 20 and 30 cm/s and 26.9% O2 at 76.1 kPa (Saffire-V) from NTRS records; other bounds approximate.

investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction – Material Ignition and Suppression Test
investigations.finding: Radiant pre-heating (a hot neighbouring surface) widens the ignitable region in microgravity, so a material that survives a cold-wall test can ignite beside a hot panel.
investigations.hardwareRule: Add an external radiant-flux axis to ignition qualification; require ignition maps at habitat O2 and pressure, not a single cold-wall point.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: ignition-and-extinction maps versus flow and radiant flux guide duct-insulation and damper-placement decisions near hot equipment.
investigations.basis: Approximate. MIST maps ignition and extinction of PMMA cylinders versus flow, O2 and radiant flux; exact matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction – Growth and Extinction Limit
investigations.finding: Fuel temperature changes flammability: a warm thick object extinguishes later than a cold one, so cabin thermal history belongs in the margin calculation.
investigations.hardwareRule: Carry a fuel-temperature term in flammability margin. A warm component is a different material than the cold coupon that was tested.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: heat-soak behaviour of thick solids informs insulated gear that stays below ignition temperature of trapped fuels during prolonged exposure.
investigations.basis: Sourced: 4 cm PMMA spheres in 0.2–80 cm/s flow and 13–28% O2 at one atmosphere (NTRS 20240007628).

investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction – Residence Time Driven Flame Spread
investigations.finding: Theory predicts steady spread cannot be sustained on fuel beyond a critical thickness even at high O2, so thickness is a hidden safety lever in microgravity.
investigations.hardwareRule: Track fuel thickness as a first-class material attribute and prefer thick-section cabin plastics where function allows.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: thickness-dependent burning gives alarm firmware a physical reason to expect different smoke onset signatures from thin films versus bulk plastics.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Thin PMMA sheets with pressure varied along the normoxic curve; exact matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction – Spacecraft Materials Microgravity Research on Flammability (SMuRF)
investigations.finding: Real spacecraft materials, not only PMMA, are being burned at habitat atmospheres, so 1g certification gaps can be quantified per material.
investigations.hardwareRule: Maintain a per-material microgravity flammability table and flag every item whose 1g pass margin is under ~3 oxygen points.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: flat-sheet spread data on technical fabrics supports lightweight layered garments tested for flame growth, not only char length.
investigations.basis: Approximate. 30 cm × 5 cm flat thin samples; test matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.finding: Burns lasted minutes with no airflow at all in crew-vehicle atmospheres, so "nothing is moving the air" is not a safe assumption.
investigations.hardwareRule: Do not treat zero ventilation as a quench guarantee in enriched atmospheres; pair HVAC park with active suppression.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: quiescent burning in enriched air supports shelter-in-place zones where fans stop but fire suppression must stay armed.
investigations.basis: Partly sourced: quiescent burns of minutes in crew-vehicle atmospheres; O2 up to 40% from ISS status reports. Pressure approximate.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Burning Rate Emulator, Part 2
investigations.finding: High-oxygen, reduced-pressure burns extend flammability beyond what ambient-pressure Earth methods capture.
investigations.hardwareRule: Require flammability screening at the exact habitat pressure and O2; do not interpolate from sea-level tests.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: oxygen-enriched burn behaviour matters for gear used near medical oxygen and hyperbaric rooms.
investigations.basis: Partly sourced: a 40% O2 / 60% N2 supply was used for BRE part 2. Pressure approximate.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Electric Field Flames
investigations.finding: Electric fields can steer and stabilise small flames, which is a candidate lever for active flame control in a habitat.
investigations.hardwareRule: Evaluate electrode-based flame steering as a low-mass supplement to mist suppression near critical avionics.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: field-sensitive flame behaviour hints at ion-based early detection that responds to incipient flames faster than smoke.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Small diffusion flame in an applied electric field, quiescent air.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame)
investigations.finding: Without buoyancy the flame structure, soot formation and sensor response are set by coflow speed and diluent, not by gravity.
investigations.hardwareRule: Calibrate flame sensors against microgravity coflow flames, since 1g teardrop signatures do not transfer.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: clean, laminar soot-formation data improves models that separate cooking particles from true combustion smoke.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Coflow speeds estimated; exact matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
investigations.finding: The ghostly blue spherical flame is the true no-buoyancy baseline: it is dim, slow and easy for cameras tuned to yellow flames to miss.
investigations.hardwareRule: Add blue-band (CH and OH emission) flame sensing alongside soot-luminosity cameras.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: blue, low-soot flames radiate differently; this informs thermal-imaging calibration for crews reading dim fires.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Quiescent spherical flame; exact matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Flame Design
investigations.finding: Soot yield changes sharply with where the diluent is added, which changes smoke signature and detector response.
investigations.hardwareRule: Characterise smoke from diluted-fuel scenarios when specifying optical detector thresholds.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: soot-versus-diluent maps help firmware recognise low-soot fires that conventional photoelectric alarms under-read.
investigations.note: The brief named "ACME FIST". No NASA or PSI record with that name was found, so this confirmed ACME investigation (Flame Design, soot control) stands in.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Quiescent flames with diluent supplied with the fuel.

investigations.title: Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment
investigations.finding: The smoke point, where a flame starts to emit soot, shifts without buoyancy, changing when a fire begins to produce detectable smoke.
investigations.hardwareRule: Set the onset threshold of smoke detection from microgravity smoke-point data, not from 1g flames.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: soot-onset physics supports alarms that alert earlier on smouldering fuel and ignore steam and cooking aerosols.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Smoke-point measurements across coflow speeds.

investigations.title: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
investigations.finding: Flame liftoff and blow-off behave differently without buoyancy, which affects when ventilation extinguishes versus sustains a flame.
investigations.hardwareRule: Use microgravity liftoff data to set the upper (blow-off) flow bound of any ventilation-based mitigation.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: liftoff and blow-off speeds help bound the air velocity at which smoke-extraction fans start to extinguish rather than feed a flame.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Flame liftoff and structure versus flow.

investigations.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigations.finding: With negligible buoyancy, smoke particles have more time to coagulate into larger aggregates than 1g detectors were designed around.
investigations.hardwareRule: Specify multi-wavelength optical scatter and particle-size discrimination, tuned for large low-g aggregates, with a dust-versus-smoke classifier.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: particle-size discrimination separates smoke from dust and steam, the route to false-alarm-free home detectors.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Overheated materials in cabin air; DOI and SAME characterisation sourced from SAE.

investigations.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment – Reflight
investigations.finding: The reflight repeated the measurement with clean sample grids, so the large-aggregate finding is not a contamination artefact.
investigations.hardwareRule: Require replicate low-g smoke datasets before locking a detector threshold, and log the TEM-verified size distribution.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: a clean, replicated size distribution is the training set for machine-learning smoke classifiers that shrug off cooking fumes.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Reflight with cleaned TEM sample grids after contamination in the first run.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.finding: After the visible flame died, heptane droplets kept vaporising with an invisible cool flame. A dark chamber does not mean the fire is out.
investigations.hardwareRule: After any suppression event, verify extinction with thermal or chemiluminescence sensing, not optical flame detection, and keep agent flowing until confirmed.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: hidden low-temperature burning after the flame disappears argues for gear and thermal-camera protocols that treat a "dark" fire as live.
investigations.basis: Sourced: ambient O2 mole fraction 0.1–0.4 and 0.7–3.0 atm (Dietrich et al. 2014). Quiescent droplet.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment – 2
investigations.finding: At 1 atm and below there is a prolonged cool-flame burn that ends only at a finite droplet size; at 5 atm the flame fades gradually rather than snapping out.
investigations.hardwareRule: Schedule suppressant dwell time by pressure: low-pressure cabins need longer agent hold to outlast cool-flame burning.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: cool-flame persistence argues for holding mist and inert-gas release in server rooms and ducts well beyond visible extinction.
investigations.basis: Approximate O2 range; 1 atm and 5 atm cases described in the cited paper.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment – 2J
investigations.finding: Part of the FLEX family that exposed cool flames; the suppression lesson (visible extinction is not full extinction) carries over.
investigations.hardwareRule: Include a post-suppression hold-and-verify stage in every automated extinguishing sequence.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: confirms that crews should treat apparently extinguished compartments as live until thermal checks clear them.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Test matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.finding: Proved the measurement concept needed for smoke work: a commercial particle counter can size aerosols in orbit.
investigations.hardwareRule: Reuse flight-proven condensation particle counting as the second channel beside optical scatter in a dual-channel smoke sensor.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: low-cost particle counting is the hardware path to alarms that report particle size, not just obscuration.
investigations.note: The brief named "CFE". In NASA catalogues CFE is the Capillary Flow Experiment (fluid physics), not combustion, so the PSI-listed DAFT stands in.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Ambient cabin air, six hours of operation.

investigations.title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test – 2
investigations.finding: Follow-up feasibility data tightens how reliably a cabin sensor can tell background dust from the onset of smoke.
investigations.hardwareRule: Maintain a dust-background baseline per module and alarm on departures from it, not on a fixed obscuration level.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Smart smoke alarms: per-room dust baselines cut nuisance alarms near construction work and kitchens.
investigations.note: The brief named "FEANIX". No NASA or PSI combustion record with that name was found, so the PSI-listed DAFT-2 stands in.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Follow-up feasibility test; matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI)
investigations.finding: Cool flames burn at low temperature with almost no visible light, so they can survive suppression that a camera reports as success.
investigations.hardwareRule: Pair optical flame sensors with a thermal or UV/IR channel that can see sub-visible burning.
investigations.earthSpinoff: Firefighter PPE: thermal cameras that can see non-luminous burning change how crews clear a compartment safely.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Droplet cool-flame regime; exact matrix not verified here.

investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.finding: Cool diffusion flames of gaseous fuels appeared without any enhancement, so spontaneous low-temperature burning is possible in a spacecraft.
investigations.hardwareRule: Do not assume low-temperature burning needs an ignition aid; qualify suppression against cool-flame reignition for 10 minutes.
investigations.earthSpinoff: High-rise HVAC smoke control: cool-flame reignition risk argues for sustained inert-gas hold times in enclosed plant rooms.
investigations.note: The brief named "ZBOT/Combustion". ZBOT is the Zero Boil-Off Tank fluids experiment, not a combustion investigation, so ACME CFI-G (gaseous cool flames) stands in.
investigations.basis: Approximate. Quiescent gaseous cool diffusion flames without added heat, plasma or ozone.
